newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY LOCKS IN JUST BELOW RESISTANCE, SEEN IDLE.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY LOCKS IN JUST BELOW RESISTANCE, SEEN IDLE.

text.p: The Polish zloty locked into its familiar position just below central bank enforced resistance at 1.5 percent from parity in early Friday trade with no large orders expected to push it higher or lower later today.
Dealers said the market would likely track dollar/mark moves all day, staying a fraction below intervention levels.
"Spreads are tight and market turnover seems destined to remain low," said Jaroslaw Dryjski, dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
"Perhaps players are thinking twice about trying their luck on Friday the 13th -- a day when strange things sometimes happen," he added jokingly.
At 0845 GMT the zloty was at 1.50/1.46 percent from parity, slightly weaker than 1.52/1.45 percent at opening.
It was at 3.2373/83 to the dollar and at 1.8728/38 to the mark, against opening's 3.2240/48 and 1.8715/25 respectively.

Dealers said a rigid zloty ceiling at 1.5 percent from parity and no interest rate cut expectations would probably keep speculative foreign capital sidelined in the near-term despite expectations of yield growth on Polish treasuries.
"The central bank is not likely to let the zloty gain within its trading band or cut the crawling-peg (devaluation factor), so foreigners are watching for now," one dealer said.
The zloty's parity rate is presently devalued one percent per month against a basket of five Western currencies.

On the money market one-day rates inched up in morning trade, but continued to straddle the central bank's main 14-day reverse repo rate of 22.15 percent with no further upward potential seen on Friday, dealers said.
Overnight rates were at 22.05/22.20 percent, up from 21.95/22.15 percent at 0630 GMT. Tomorrow/next rates were at 22.10/22.30 percent, flat from Thursday's close.
